title: Plane Shapes: Symmetry, Lines, Cardinal Points and Angles
seo_title: Symmetry, Lines and Angles – Primary 4 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Identify lines of symmetry; draw horizontal and vertical lines; identify cardinal points; identify right, acute and obtuse angles. (summary of the NERDC Primary 4 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 4 maths worksheets on lines of symmetry, horizontal and vertical lines, the cardinal points of the compass and right, acute and obtuse angles. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A line of symmetry makes two matching halves
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A line of symmetry divides a shape into two halves that fit exactly on each other when folded.
  • A horizontal line goes straight across; a vertical line goes straight up and down.
  • The cardinal points are North, East, South and West. Between them are North-East, South-East, South-West and North-West.
  • A right angle is a quarter turn (90°). An acute angle is smaller; an obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight line.

Examples

Example

Facing North, make a quarter turn clockwise

N → E

Answer: East

Example

How many lines of symmetry does a square have?

2 through the sides, 2 through the corners

Answer: 4

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Taking a diagonal of a rectangle as a line of symmetryFold it: the halves do not match.
Mixing up clockwise and anticlockwiseClockwise goes the way the hands of a clock turn.
Thinking a bigger drawing means a bigger angleThe size of an angle is the amount of turn.

items.q: Fold the square along the dashed line. Is the dashed line a line of symmetry?
c: Yes, it cuts it in half
No, same size but they do not match
items.e: The line is not in the middle, so one part is bigger than the other. When you fold, the small part cannot cover the big part, so it is not a line of symmetry.

items.q: Fold the rectangle along the dashed line. Is the dashed line a line of symmetry?
c: No, same size but they do not match
No, it must go up and down
items.e: Fold on the line: the two halves land exactly on each other, so it is a line of symmetry. The line goes across. A line of symmetry can go in any direction, not only up and down.

Yes, it cuts it in half
items.e: The line cuts the rectangle into 2 parts of the same size, but when you fold on it the corners stick out and the halves do not land on each other. Cutting a shape in half is not enough: the halves must match when folded.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
items.e: A square has 4 lines of symmetry: 1 up and down, 1 across, and 2 along the diagonals, corner to corner. Do not forget the diagonals.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle have?
items.e: A rectangle has 2 lines of symmetry: up and down and across, through the middles of the sides. The diagonals cut it in half, but folded on a diagonal the corners stick out.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a triangle with 3 equal sides have?
items.e: Each line goes from a corner to the middle of the opposite side. There are 3 corners, so there are 3 lines.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a triangle with 2 equal sides have?
items.e: Only the line from the top corner down to the middle of the bottom side works, so there is 1 line.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a triangle with 3 different sides have?
items.e: All 3 sides have different lengths, so no fold makes the halves match. There are 0 lines of symmetry.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a circle have?
items.e: Every line through the centre of a circle folds it into matching halves. There are infinitely many lines.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rhombus have?
items.e: A rhombus that is not a square has 2 lines of symmetry, and both go corner to corner (its diagonals). Lines through the middles of the sides do not work.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a parallelogram have?
items.e: A slanted parallelogram has 0 lines of symmetry. Its diagonals cut it in half, but folded the corners stick out.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a kite have?
items.e: Only the long line from the top corner to the bottom corner works, so a kite has 1 line of symmetry.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a trapezium with 2 equal slanted sides have?
items.e: Only the up-and-down line through the middles of the top and bottom works. A line across does not, because the top is shorter than the bottom. 1 line.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for this angle?
items.e: Compare with a right angle (90°). This angle is smaller than a right angle, so about 30° fits. (It is 28°.) About 150° is wider than a right angle, so it cannot be the answer.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for this angle?
items.e: The rays almost make a straight line (180°), so it is about 180°. (It is 170°.) About 10° is a tiny angle, almost closed.

items.q: An angle measures 135°. What kind of angle is it?
items.e: 135° is more than 90° and less than 180°, so it is obtuse.

items.q: Which angle measure is acute?
items.e: Acute means less than 90°. Only 75° is less than 90°.

items.q: Which could be the measure of an obtuse angle?
items.e: An obtuse angle is between 90° and 180°. 140° is the only one in that range.

items.q: How many right angles make a straight angle?
items.e: 90° + 90° = 180°, so 2 right angles make a straight angle. (4 right angles make a full turn.)

items.q: Omar says a 100° angle is acute because 100 is a small number. Is he right?
items.e: 100° is more than 90°, so the angle is wider than a right angle. That makes it obtuse.

items.q: An angle measures 180°. What kind of angle is it?
items.e: 180° is a half turn. The rays make a straight line, so it is a straight angle.
